standard_prerequisites.name: Functor precategory
standard_prerequisites.statement: B^A has functors as objects and natural transformations as morphisms, with composition and identity defined componentwise.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the precategory whose hom-types must be shown to be sets.

standard_prerequisites.name: Category
standard_prerequisites.statement: A category is a precategory in which every identity type of the object type is equivalent to the type of isomorphisms via idtoiso.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the goal of the theorem.

standard_prerequisites.name: Function extensionality and isotoid
standard_prerequisites.statement: Two functions are identified by a homotopy, and isotoid is the inverse of idtoiso on the object type of a category.
standard_prerequisites.use: They are used to build the candidate inverse of idtoiso at source lines 362-363 and to check the two round trips.

core_obligations: Reduce the goal to showing that idtoiso : (F = G) -> (F ~ G) is an equivalence for functors F, G : A -> B (source line 359).

Given a natural isomorphism gamma, produce an identity F = G: apply isotoid componentwise and use function extensionality to identify the object maps (source lines 361-363), then show the remaining functor axioms agree because they are mere propositions (source lines 365-372), the computation of transport being exactly the retained transport lemma.
Check the first round trip on identities p, q : F = G by reducing to the object level, where the construction is definitional on p (source lines 375-379).
Check the second round trip on natural isomorphisms gamma by testing componentwise and using that isotoid and idtoiso are mutually inverse (source lines 381-385).

proof_roadmap.step: Build the candidate inverse from a natural isomorphism.
Agree on the functor axioms using the retained transport computation.
Second round trip on natural isomorphisms.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Theorem 9.2.5 at source lines 353-357: if A is a precategory and B is a category then the functor precategory B^A is a category. The author's proof (source lines 358-386) is a three-stage argument. It first constructs an inverse to idtoiso from a natural isomorphism, using isotoid componentwise and function extensionality for the object maps (lines 361-363); it then has to show that the resulting identity matches the functor structure, which is where the retained transport computation is invoked, since transporting a morphism along isotoid of the components is conjugation by those isomorphisms and naturality identifies the result with the other functor (lines 365-372); and finally both round trips are checked, the first by reducing to the object level (lines 375-379) and the second componentwise using that isotoid and idtoiso are inverse (lines 381-385). The statement is one line and records none of the three stages.
